findings.title: O(N²) performance in _is_in_fenced_block called line-by-line in _detect_cosmetic_violations
findings.why: This helper walks from line 0 to idx on every call. In _detect_cosmetic_violations (line 251), it's called once per line in a loop (lines 251-253), producing O(N²) complexity for an N-line file. For a 500-line roadmap, this is ~125K iterations; for 1000 lines, ~500K. The same helper is reused in all transform functions (_apply_trailing_whitespace_fix line 583, _apply_smart_quote_fold line 616, _apply_table_padding_fix line 640, _apply_resource_subsection_rewrites line 712), though transforms run only when violations are detected.
findings.recommendation: Precompute a boolean mask in a single forward pass at the start of _detect_cosmetic_violations and each transform function. Store the result (e.g., `in_fenced: list[bool]`) and index into it O(1) per line. This changes the overall complexity from O(N²) to O(N).

findings.title: Potential TOCTOU race when cosmetic remediator writes between gate_passed calls
findings.evidence:
gate_target = _gate_target(step.output_file)
passed, reason = gate_passed(gate_target, step.gate)
...
if config.allow_cosmetic_remediation and config.cosmetic_remediator is not None:
    ...
    for sc in step.gate.semantic_checks:
        sc_result = sc.check_fn(gate_target.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ...
    config.cosmetic_remediator(gate_target, gate_name, reason or "", step_id=step.id)
    ...
    recheck_passed, recheck_reason = gate_passed(gate_target, step.gate)
findings.why: At line 10 (diff numbering), executor.py reads gate_target and calls gate_passed. If the gate fails, the remediation lane (lines 30-43, diff) re-reads gate_target.read_text() at line 36 to identify which semantic_check failed, then the remediator writes the file (cli/roadmap/executor.py:3177 via output_file.write_text), then gate_passed is called again. Between the initial gate_passed and the semantic_check loop, another thread/process could modify the file (though unlikely in single-process pipeline executor). More realistically, if the compressed sidecar resolution (_gate_target logic at executor.py:32-35) resolves differently between calls due to filesystem races, the semantic_check loop reads a different file than gate_passed saw.
findings.recommendation: Cache the content string after the first read (line 10) and pass it into the remediator's classify_gate_failure instead of having the remediator re-read. This also improves performance by avoiding redundant I/O. Alternatively, document that the executor is single-threaded and this is not a concern.

findings.title: Encoding inconsistency: roadmap adapter uses explicit encoding, pipeline executor.py semantic_check loop does not specify errors= kwarg
findings.why: In executor.py line 36 (diff), read_text(encoding='utf-8') is called without errors= kwarg. If gate_target contains invalid UTF-8 (e.g., binary corruption, Latin-1 leftover), this raises UnicodeDecodeError. Compare: cli/roadmap/executor.py:3164 and cli/roadmap/executor.py:3177 both use encoding='utf-8' consistently; compression.py:1174 uses encoding='utf-8'; existing gate helpers like _parse_frontmatter implicitly rely on pre-decoded str. However, other read sites in the codebase (e.g., .dev/eval-workspaces/*/grade.py:19) use errors='replace' for graceful degradation.
findings.recommendation: Add errors='replace' to the read_text call at line 36 (diff) for consistency with repo's defensive read patterns (seen in audit/reachability.py, install_mcp.py:126-128, and .dev/ scripts). Alternatively, wrap in try/except UnicodeDecodeError and classify as semantic violation.

findings.title: Windows line-ending compatibility: _apply_blank_line_collapse uses \n{3,} regex without \r support
findings.why:
The regex `
{3,}` matches 3+ consecutive LF characters. On Windows, a file with CRLF line endings (`
`) will have `



` for 4 blank lines. The pattern `
{3,}` matches the 4 LFs but leaves the 4 CRs untouched, producing `

` (malformed). The repo's other file-handling code (compression.py:1174, roadmap/executor.py:604-605, install_hooks.py:439) all use encoding='utf-8' with no explicit newline= kwarg, meaning Python's universal newline mode applies on read (normalizes to 
) but writes preserve the platform default. If a Windows contributor runs the roadmap pipeline, the output file may have CRLF, and this transform will corrupt it.
findings.recommendation: Change regex to `(\r?\n){3,}` and replacement to `\1\1` (two instances of the captured newline sequence) to preserve the line-ending style. Or normalize all content to LF at read time and back to CRLF at write time if needed. Cross-reference: gates.py does not exhibit this issue because _template_sections_present (line 927-1015) uses splitlines() which is line-ending-agnostic.

findings.title: Code duplication: _strip_section_numbering duplicates gates._normalize_heading regex without reuse
findings.why: The comment at line 158 explicitly states this "mirrors gates._normalize_heading" but reimplements the regex. gates._normalize_heading (line 919-924) does the same prefix strip plus lowercase. The remediator needs case-preserved output, so it can't call _normalize_heading directly. However, the regex is duplicated. If the numbering pattern changes (e.g., to support roman numerals), both must be updated. This is a minor maintainability issue.
findings.recommendation: Extract the regex pattern to a shared constant (e.g., _SECTION_NUMBERING_PATTERN in gates.py) and import it into cosmetic_remediator.py. Or factor out a gates.strip_section_numbering(text, lowercase=True) helper that both modules call.

findings.title: Potential false positive: \xa0 (non-breaking space) in _NONCANONICAL_DASH_PATTERN may match legitimate body text
findings.why: The pattern includes standalone `\xa0` (non-breaking space) as a dash substitute. This is intentional per the design (no-break-space replacing a dash is a common drift), but `\xa0` can appear legitimately in body text (e.g., "M 1" in HTML-converted markdown, French typography rules with nbsp before punctuation). If a user writes "Section 1 — M 1" with an nbsp between M and 1, the C3 detector (line 303) will flag the line as having a non-canonical dash even though the heading stem might not match a required stem. The detector short-circuits correctly (line 302 checks stem_lower in _REQUIRED_STEMS_LOWER first), but the pattern search at line 303 runs on the full line text, not just the separator region.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the _NONCANONICAL_DASH_PATTERN search to the separator region extracted by _h3_stem_and_suffix (between stem and suffix) rather than searching the entire line. This prevents false positives in heading text that legitimately contains nbsp. Alternatively, document this as acceptable drift (nbsp in a heading is always canonicalized away) and leave as-is.

findings.title: Ordering issue: _h3_stem_and_suffix processes canonical separators before _strip_section_numbering, allowing edge case
findings.why: The caller at line 292 in _detect_cosmetic_violations does `heading_body = _strip_section_numbering(line[4:])` BEFORE calling `stem, suffix = _h3_stem_and_suffix(heading_body)`. However, _h3_stem_and_suffix itself tries canonical separators like ` -- ` first (line 174). If a heading is `### 1. Risk Assessment -- M1 -- extra`, the strip removes `1. `, leaving `Risk Assessment -- M1 -- extra`. The partition at line 176 on ` -- ` will match the FIRST occurrence, splitting into stem=`Risk Assessment`, suffix=`-- M1 -- extra`. The detector logic (line 294) then lowercases stem and checks membership. This is correct for the TUIBBS case (no section numbering, single separator). But if a heading has BOTH numbering AND multiple dash occurrences, the stem extraction may be wrong. Trace: `### 2.3. Integration Points u2014 M2 -- see note` → after strip_section_numbering → `Integration Points u2014 M2 -- see note` → _h3_stem_and_suffix tries ` -- ` first, finds it, partitions into (`Integration Points u2014 M2`, `-- see note`) → stem_lower = `integration points u2014 m2` which is NOT in _REQUIRED_STEMS_LOWER → C3/C2 don't fire → C4 might fire if this were a ##. Actually C3 checks the original line (line 303), not the post-partition stem, so this is safe. Re-analysis: the partition logic is safe because the detector checks stem_lower membership first, and the transform at line 548 does _strip_section_numbering again before partitioning. However, the comment at line 167 says "strip section numbering first" which is misleading because the helper itself does not strip—it assumes the caller did.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the comment at line 167 or call _strip_section_numbering inside _h3_stem_and_suffix for robustness. Alternatively, add a unit test for the edge case `### 2.3. Integration Points u2014 M2 -- extra` to verify correct parsing.

findings.title: Missing --allow-cosmetic-remediation documentation in user-facing docs
findings.why: The PR adds two new CLI flags (--allow-cosmetic-remediation and --strict-no-remediation) with detailed help text. However, no user-facing documentation file (docs/user-guide/, docs/reference/, README) is updated to mention them. Developers running `superclaude roadmap run --help` will see the flags, but documentation readers won't know they exist. Cross-referencing: docs/developer-guide/technical-architecture.md does not list CLI flags for individual commands; docs/reference/ may have a roadmap command reference that should be updated.
findings.recommendation: Add a section to docs/user-guide/ or docs/reference/ documenting the new flags, when to use --strict-no-remediation (high-stakes runs), and the default behavior (cosmetic auto-fix enabled). Include an example of a cosmetic vs semantic failure.

findings.title: Test coverage gap: no test for Windows CRLF line endings in _apply_blank_line_collapse
findings.evidence:
def test_c7_blank_line_collapse(self):
    content = (
        ...
        "# T

## Executive Summary
foo




"  # 4 blank lines
        ...
    )
    cl = classify_gate_failure(content, _GATE, "x", step_id="s1")
    assert cl.is_pure_cosmetic is True
    new, _ = apply_cosmetic_remediations(content, cl)
    assert "


" not in new
findings.why:
The test at line 205 verifies blank-line collapse for LF line endings. No test covers CRLF (`
`) line endings, which are the default on Windows. Given the regex issue identified in finding #4 (cosmetic_remediator.py:604 uses `
{3,}` without `` support), this test gap means the bug would not be caught. The test suite's inline markdown uses `
` literals (line 208), not `
`.
findings.recommendation:
Add a test `test_c7_blank_line_collapse_crlf` that constructs content with `



` and verifies the transform preserves CRLF. Alternatively, mark as known limitation and document that Windows users should configure Git to auto-convert CRLF to LF.

findings.title: Test coverage gap: no test for nested fenced blocks or inline code with backticks
findings.why: The _is_in_fenced_block helper (cosmetic_remediator.py:204) counts ``` lines and uses parity to determine block state. It does not handle nested code blocks (markdown within markdown, e.g., a fenced block containing a ````` five-backtick fence) or inline code with triple backticks (e.g., text ``` inline ``` text on the same line). The test file has no test for these edge cases. If a roadmap's Risk Assessment section includes an inline code snippet like "use `--flag` to enable", and the line has trailing whitespace, the detector at line 269 (cosmetic_remediator.py) should flag C6, but if the line also has "```" earlier, the fenced-block check might mis-classify it.
findings.recommendation: Add tests: (1) a fenced block containing a heading-like line with trailing whitespace (should not be flagged), (2) inline triple-backticks on a line with trailing whitespace (should be flagged as C6 because inline code is not a fenced block), (3) a closing ``` on the same line as an opening ``` (empty block—parity logic should handle it).

findings.title: Test coverage gap: no test for multi-milestone document where C2/C3 fires in later milestones
findings.evidence:
def _content_with_milestone(
    subsections: list[str],
    *,
    mid: str = "1",
    ...
) -> str:
    """Assemble a minimal roadmap-ish markdown with one milestone."""
    h2 = f"## M{mid}: Foundation\n\nObjective: x | Duration: y | Exit: z\n\n"
    ...
findings.why: The test helper _content_with_milestone builds a document with a single milestone (M1 by default). The detector logic in _current_milestone_id (cosmetic_remediator.py:188) walks backward to find the enclosing ## M{N}: and _detect_cosmetic_violations (line 296) uses this to scope H3s. No test verifies behavior when a document has M1, M2, M3 and only M2 has a cosmetic defect (e.g., `### Risk Assessment` with no suffix under M2, but M1 and M3 are clean). This is important because the transformer's h2_re loop (line 524) maintains current_mid state across milestones.
findings.recommendation: Add a test with 3 milestones where M1 is clean, M2 has a C2 violation, M3 is clean. Verify the transform only rewrites M2's heading and preserves M1/M3.

findings.title: Layering: cli/pipeline/models.py imports Protocol from typing, not from cli/roadmap
findings.evidence:
from typing import Callable, Literal, Optional, Protocol

class CosmeticRemediator(Protocol):
    """Pluggable cosmetic-failure remediator (see cli/roadmap/cosmetic_remediator.py)."""
    ...
findings.why: NFR-007 states `cli/pipeline/*` MUST NOT import from `cli/sprint/*` or `cli/roadmap/*`. The new CosmeticRemediator Protocol is defined in pipeline/models.py (correct—no import violation) but the docstring at line 18 references "see cli/roadmap/cosmetic_remediator.py". This is a documentation cross-reference, not a code import, so it does not violate NFR-007. However, it creates a conceptual coupling: pipeline/models.py now documents a roadmap-specific implementation. If sprint wanted to use a different remediator protocol, this docstring would be misleading. The Protocol itself is generic (takes output_file, gate_name, failure_reason, step_id), so it's architecturally sound.
findings.recommendation: Rephrase the docstring to "Pluggable cosmetic-failure remediator. Consumers (e.g., roadmap pipeline) may inject an implementation via PipelineConfig.cosmetic_remediator." Remove the explicit path reference to maintain layering separation. Alternatively, leave as-is and document that this is acceptable because it's a doc-only reference, not a code dependency.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Cosmetic remediator assumes UTF-8 encoding throughout; no handling for BOM or alternative encodings
cross_cutting_observations.why: All file reads in the remediator flow (executor.py:36, roadmap/executor.py:3164, 3177) use encoding='utf-8' without BOM handling. If a Windows user saves a roadmap with UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF), the BOM appears as U+FEFF at the start of content and will break frontmatter parsing (`content.startswith('---\n')` at cosmetic_remediator.py:410 returns False). The repo's compression.py:1174 and gates.py (via _parse_frontmatter) also assume UTF-8 with no BOM stripping. This is a cross-cutting issue: the entire roadmap pipeline is BOM-intolerant.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add BOM detection and stripping at the read boundary (either in _gate_target or in the remediator adapter). Python's codecs.BOM_UTF8 can be checked. Alternatively, document that roadmap files must be UTF-8 without BOM and add a pre-flight check in the executor.

cross_cutting_observations.title: No graceful degradation path when cosmetic remediator raises unexpected exception
cross_cutting_observations.why: The roadmap adapter at executor.py:3162-3179 wraps classify_gate_failure and apply_cosmetic_remediations in a try/except that catches OSError (line 3165) and returns (False, []). However, if the classifier or transformer raises any other exception (e.g., re.error from a malformed regex, AttributeError from None dereference, or a bug in the transform logic), the exception propagates uncaught and halts the pipeline. The generic executor at pipeline/executor.py:48 does not wrap the remediator call in a try/except, so an exception in the remediator's __call__ will crash the step. This is a defense-in-depth gap: a cosmetic-remediation bug should not prevent the pipeline from running with strict mode (--strict-no-remediation).
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Wrap the remediator call at pipeline/executor.py:48 in a broad try/except that logs the exception and treats it as (False, [])—i.e., remediation failed, proceed to normal FAIL handling. Alternatively, wrap at the roadmap adapter level (executor.py:3162) with `except Exception as exc` and log a warning.

notes_for_orchestrator: Completed systematic review covering all focus areas. Performance finding #1 (O(N²) _is_in_fenced_block) is the highest-impact issue. TOCTOU finding #2 is theoretical but worth documenting. Windows line-ending issue #4 is a real cross-platform bug. Test coverage gaps (#9-#11) are standard quality bar issues. Architecture finding #12 is a nit (doc-only coupling). No security, data-integrity, or resource-leak issues found. The PR's root-cause fix (u2014→-- in template) is sound. The defense-in-depth cosmetic-remediation lane is well-designed but has the performance and edge-case issues noted above.
